test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 13 Sept, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that gives their correct logical sequence and forms a meaningful sentence.

In November, Lakshman fell (P) / with fever (Q) / seriously ill (R) and pneumonia (S).
solution:
The correct answer is** Option (2)** i.e. **P, R, Q, S**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence begins with "In November, Lakshman fell," which is correctly indicated by **part (P).**** **
 
• Following the subject, "seriously ill" **(R)** continues the logical sequence, making it clear how Lakshman fell.
 
• **The next part,** "with fever" **(Q)** adds more detail about Lakshman's condition.
 
• **Ending with **"and pneumonia" **(S)** completes the sentence by specifying the illnesses.

Therefore, the correct answer is **P, R, Q, S.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (P, Q, S, R):** This option starts with "In November, Lakshman fell with fever and pneumonia seriously ill," which is not grammatically correct.
 
• **Option 3 (P, Q, R, S):** This option starts with "In November, Lakshman fell with fever seriously ill and pneumonia," which is not logically correct as the structure is awkward.
 
• **Option 4 (R, Q, S, P):** This option starts with "seriously ill with fever and pneumonia In November, Lakshman fell," which does not make sense contextually.
